page: Vultr voc-g-32c-128gb-640s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU configuration consists of 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 640 GB local NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark evaluations show strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng tests placing both metrics in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with large-block read-only and write bandwidth tests reaching top-tier status in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, image processing, and Passmark CPU tests also rank in the top 25%. However, single-threaded compression and decompression, Geekbench compiling, and static web serving throughput remain in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high-speed NVMe storage provide a balanced hardware profile for multi-threaded workloads. While the server offers top-tier memory bandwidth, its database operations and Passmark memory scores align with average-tier performance, indicating potential latency tradeoffs under specific database access patterns. This server is suited for multi-threaded data processing, image processing, Redis caching layers, and medium-scale LLM text generation tasks.
